title: RFK Jr.'s Son Conor Kennedy Placed on Russia's Wanted List Over Ukraine Service
excerpt: A Moscow court authorized the arrest in absentia of the 32-year-old Kennedy scion, who secretly fought for Ukraine's International Legion in 2022 and now faces up to 10 years in a Russian prison.
body:
• Conor Kennedy, 32, the son of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., has been placed on Russia's international wanted list.
  • A Moscow court authorized his arrest in absentia on August 12 on charges of acting as a mercenary for Ukraine's armed forces.
  • Kennedy secretly traveled to Ukraine in 2022 and served on the northeastern front line with the International Legion.
  • If detained, he faces seven to 10 years in a Russian prison under Article 353 of the Russian Criminal Code.

Moscow Court Orders Arrest

Conor Kennedy, the 32-year-old son of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., has been placed on Russia's international wanted list after a Moscow court authorized his arrest in absentia, according to Russian state media outlet TASS.

https://x.com/NEWSMAX/status/2090249969257287823

The Basmanny District Court of Moscow issued the order on August 12, charging Kennedy with "participation of a mercenary in an armed conflict or military action" under Article 353 of the Russian Criminal Code. The charge carries a sentence of seven to 10 years in prison if he is successfully detained.

Kennedy's legal team challenged the decision but a Russian appeals court upheld it during a closed hearing, TASS reported.

A Secret Trip to the Front Lines

The charge stems from Kennedy's secret trip to Ukraine in 2022, when — while on a break from his law studies at Georgetown University — he enlisted in the International Legion of Ukraine and served on the Kharkiv front.

Kennedy revealed his participation in an Instagram post in October 2022, disclosing that he had told only one person his real name and kept his enlistment secret from his family.

"Like many people, I was deeply moved by what I saw happening in Ukraine over the past year. I wanted to help. When I heard about Ukraine's International Legion, I knew I was going, and I went to the embassy to enlist the next day."

— Conor Kennedy, in an October 2022 Instagram post

Kennedy admitted he had no military experience and "wasn't a great shot" but said he learned quickly and was willing to die for Ukraine's cause. "My time in Ukraine wasn't long but I saw a lot and I felt a lot. I liked being a soldier, more than I had expected," he wrote.

His father later said he began to suspect his son's whereabouts only after credit card charges appeared in Poland and Ukraine. RFK Jr. said he was "very proud" of his son.

A Kennedy on Moscow's List

The wanted listing places a member of one of America's most prominent political families on a collision course with Moscow at a time when the Russia-Ukraine war continues with no resolution in sight. Conor Kennedy is the grandson of former U.S. Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy and the great-nephew of former President John F. Kennedy.

Russia has targeted multiple foreign volunteers who fought for Ukraine, accusing them of acting as mercenaries. The International Legion, established after Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, provided a formal pathway for foreign volunteers to serve with Ukraine's military.

Kennedy, now a practicing lawyer, is not at immediate risk of arrest in the United States. Russia's wanted list, however, means he could face detention if he travels to countries with extradition agreements with Moscow or cooperative law enforcement arrangements.

Political Implications

The case adds a personal dimension to the Kennedy family's already complex relationship with the Trump administration's Russia policy. RFK Jr. serves as Health Secretary in President Trump's cabinet, and the administration has faced criticism for its approach to the Ukraine conflict.

Conor Kennedy described the foreign volunteers he fought alongside as "freedom fighters" and wrote that "this war will shape the fate of democracy in this century." He has not publicly commented on the Russian charges.
